archetype: Ranged single-target burst archer. Damage is concentrated in Snipe and its Empowered/Ultimate follow-ups rather than in a hold-to-fire main attack, with Piercing Arrow as the line-clear skill.

linkSkill.name: Adventurer's Curiosity
linkSkill.effect: At master level: Monster Collection add chance +50%, Critical Rate +15%, Damage +6% (the Damage component appears at Lv. 7). The wiki notes the bonus is multiplicative rather than additive. Stacks up to 3 times, once per unique Explorer Bowman job character on the world - so it is shared with Bow Master and Pathfinder, not exclusive to Marksman.

legionEffect.notes: NamuWiki's KMS page treats the class's own crit-rate union effect as combining with crit-rate legion picks specifically because of the Vicious Shot conversion (see gearingNotes).

vMatrix.priorityNote: NO SOURCE RANKS MARKSMAN BOOST NODES AGAINST ONE ANOTHER, so no ranking is stored. An earlier version of this file shipped an ordered `priority` array; array position was doing work no source supports, and the array has been removed. Grandis Library's own trio block says in as many words 'Any combination of these skills are good'. What IS sourced is a two-band split (nodeBands below) and trio membership (trios below). Nothing in this section is ordered - treat every array here as a set.

nodeBands.grandisDefinition: Boost Nodes that unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery and are skills that are frequently used
nodeBands.why: Read directly from the Grandis Library Marksman page: its boost-node data groups node indices 0-3 as `primary`, and the four Primary blocks render in the Primary colour. The page's own legend gives the rationale - a Primary node is one that unlocks a 6th Job HEXA Mastery and is frequently used. That is the same set as the four HEXA mastery cores recorded under hexa.nodeInventory.masteryCores, which is the one genuinely mechanical reason to favour these four.

nodeBands.grandisDefinition: Boost Nodes that don't unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery but are still used
nodeBands.why: Grandis groups node indices 4-5 as `secondary`. IMPORTANT: Secondary is NOT a discouragement. The page states 'Nodes categorized as Primary and Secondary are recommended to be upgraded'. The OTHER band - the one Grandis defines as 'do not need to be upgraded or has least priority' - is EMPTY for Marksman.

vMatrix.nodeBandsNote: These bands are a recommendation-vs-not split with a HEXA-mastery rationale, NOT a damage-priority ranking, and the band order above must not be read as one beyond 'Primary unlocks a HEXA Mastery, Secondary does not'. Both bands are recommended for upgrade by the source. A previous version of this file inverted the bands (calling Bolt Burst/Frostprey and Final Attack/High Speed Shot lower-tier, and Covering Fire 'lowest tier') and also treated the bands as a priority ordering; both errors are corrected here.

skills: Snipe (Grandis and the infographic write it Snipe/Empowered Snipe)
Piercing Arrow (written Piercing Arrow/Empowered Piercing Arrow)

That conflict was an artefact of comparing two different structures on the same page: Grandis publishes BOTH a recommended-trio block (which matches the infographic exactly) and a separate node-tier table (which describes which boost nodes exist and how they are grouped in-game). skillNodes.claim: Highest-priority V skill node for Marksman, for both bossing and levelling.
skillNodes.why: The quick-guide infographic states it verbatim: 'Split Shot is your most important skill for both Bossing and Leveling. Very High priority.' The skill's own wiki description explains the mechanism - while Split Shot is active, Full Burst Shot landed after Piercing Arrow, Snipe, either Empowered variant, Ultimate Piercing, Ultimate Snipe, HEXA High Speed Shot, Final Aim or Repeating Crossbow Cartridge splits for extra hits, so it multiplies the rest of the kit rather than adding damage of its own. NamuWiki's KMS page independently calls Split Shot (machine-translated 'Split Arrow') the skill 'which takes up most of the damage', and attributes a 20-30% damage loss at Suu to losing roughly half its uptime.
skillNodes.notes: Two independent families judge Split Shot central (Marksman Discord infographic; NamuWiki KMS). maplestorywiki supplies the mechanism and no judgement, so it is not counted toward sourceCount.

vMatrix.notes: No public Marksman class document exists. Grandis Library's per-class pages normally carry a 'Class Doc' link; the Marksman page has none (re-verified 2026-09-12: its Other Resources block links only maplestorywiki, NamuWiki and the class Discord), and its credits attribute the inner ability, hyper passive and boost node fields to the Marksman Discord. So the Grandis page and the Grandis-hosted infographics are ONE source family, not two. The only outside corroboration found for trios is mastermysty's cross-class table, which self-reports a 2024-11-21 page date and 2024-05-14 trio data - predating the v.269 boost-node regrouping (Grandis exposes a 'View Pre-V.269 Boost Nodes' toggle, direct evidence the groupings changed) - and which publishes no provenance for its trio selections. Treat the agreement on WHICH three skills matter as the solid part; treat the in-game node pairings as sourced only to the current Grandis page.

order.step: Open five different nodes at level 1 before deep-levelling any one of them
order.why: Re-read from both charts at full resolution on 2026-09-12. Each chart's first five entries are labelled Lv 1 and sit on five visually distinct node icons; from the sixth entry onward the icons start repeating with higher target levels (Lv 4, Lv 2, Lv 6 ...). So the opening move on both charts is breadth, not depth.
order.caveat: One source family (both charts are credited to the Marksman Discord), so sourceCount is 1 even though two images agree. The level labels are legible and were read directly; the identity of each node icon was NOT resolved and is deliberately not recorded.

order.step: On the FRAGMENTS-efficient chart, HEXA Stat cores are activated part-way through, not at the start
order.why: Counted directly off the chart's 13-column grid, read left to right row by row: the entries labelled Stat 1, Stat 2 and Stat 3 are the 36th, 49th and 61st of about 170 entries - after a substantial block of skill, mastery and boost investment.
order.caveat: Scoped to the fragments chart only - see the next entry. Positions re-counted at full resolution on 2026-09-12 and found exact, not approximate.

order.step: The two charts DISAGREE about when to take the first HEXA Stat, and the difference is large
order.why: The energy-efficient chart is a 9-column grid and places Stat 1 as its 8th entry, in the first row. The fragments-efficient chart places Stat 1 at entry 36. A player following the wrong chart for their server takes HEXA Stat roughly 28 steps early or late. GMS Heroic/Reboot players want the FRAGMENTS chart, because Sol Erda Fragments are the binding constraint there.
order.caveat: Both charts are Marksman Discord products, so this is one family disagreeing with itself across two optimisation targets, not two sources disagreeing. Read directly from the Stat 1 labels on both images.

That is a real coupling between two mastery nodes, which is the kind of thing an investment order gets built around - but no source found states what order to build them in, so none is recorded.
mechanicalNotes.notes: Weak by the source-count rule only. This is a mechanical reading of the skill's own effect text on the authoritative wiki, not a guide's judgement, and it was cleared by a prior adversarial pass. No recommendation is derived from it.

mechanicalNotes.why: Stated on the wiki's Marksman HEXA Enhancements section. The two class skill cores also list their own breakpoint bonuses at Lv. 10/20/30 (Final Aim: Ignore DEF and Boss Damage; Fatal Trigger: Ignore DEF and Boss Damage).

Grandis Library hosts two Marksman 6th-job charts, credited to the Marksman Discord and last checked 2026-06-25: 'Fragments Efficient' (https://grandislibrary.com/class-infographic/marksman/marksman-6th-job-fragments.png, a 13-column grid of about 170 entries) and 'Energy Efficient' (https://grandislibrary.com/class-infographic/marksman/marksman-6th-job-energy.png, a 9-column grid). Both images were re-opened at full resolution on 2026-09-12: the level labels and the Stat 1/2/3 markers are legible and were read; the individual node icons were NOT identified to a confidence level that would justify writing node names down, so no per-node order is claimed. Surface the images to the user rather than a transcription. The fragment-efficient variant is the one that matters for GMS Heroic, where Sol Erda Fragments are the binding constraint. Nothing outside the Marksman Discord family publishes any Marksman HEXA order - there is no class doc, mapledoro's '6th job leveling order' section reads 'Coming soon' (re-verified 2026-09-12), and the aggregator sites carry no Marksman-specific ordering.

hyperStats.notes: No source was found that states a Marksman hyper stat priority order. Re-checked 2026-09-12: the Grandis Library Marksman page contains no hyper stat section (nor does its Bow Master page - the string does not occur on either); the Marksman quick-guide infographic has no hyper stat block; mapledoro's Marksman page has no hyper stat section; and there is no Marksman class document. Nothing is recorded here rather than importing another class's list. The community's operative answer to hyper stat allocation is a per-character computation against a given boss rather than a fixed list - MathBro's hyper stat optimizer at https://brendonmay.github.io/hyperCalculator/ - which is a cross-class fact, not a Marksman-specific one. One Marksman-specific input to that calculation IS recorded, under gearingNotes: because of Vicious Shot, critical rate does not stop paying at 100%, so any optimizer or planner that hard-caps crit at 100% will under-rate the crit rate hyper stat for this class.

innerAbility.notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-12. An earlier version of this file claimed Grandis Library 'normally splits recommended inner ability into bossing and training and labels it by attack-speed-cap region'. The bossing/training half is true - the Grandis inner-ability data carries an optional `name` field, used on the Bow Master page as 'For Bossing' / 'For Training', and the Marksman entry has no name and is a single flat list of three lines. The region / attack-speed-cap half was INVENTED: no such field exists in the data on either page. gearingNotes:
CRITICAL RATE DOES NOT STOP PAYING AT 100%. Vicious Shot, the shared Explorer Archer 5th job skill, allows Critical Rate to exceed 100% and increases Critical Damage by a percentage of total Critical Rate - 21% of crit rate at Lv. 1 rising to 50% at Lv. 30 - for 30 seconds on a 120 second cooldown. CORRECTED 2026-09-12: an earlier version of this file glossed the wiki's exclusion clause as 'the skill's own additional crit rate is excluded from the conversion'. Vicious Shot grants no critical rate of its own. The wiki line reads 'The attack's additional Critical Rate is not applied', which means a skill's per-attack Bonus Critical Rate (the wiki prints 'Bonus Critical Rate: 100%' on a number of Marksman attacks) does not feed the conversion. The conversion therefore runs off the character's actual crit-rate stat - which strengthens the planner conclusion below, but by a different mechanism than the one previously written down. Source: maplestorywiki's Marksman skill page. NamuWiki's KMS page reaches the same practical conclusion independently, treating crit-rate inner ability lines and the crit-rate union/legion picks as valuable specifically because they convert during that window. Consequence for a planner: do not hard-cap crit rate at 100% for this class, and do not rank the crit rate hyper stat or the crit-rate inner ability line the way you would for a class that caps. NOTE THIS IS NOT A MARKSMAN-VS-BOW-MASTER DIFFERENCE - Vicious Shot is shared by both Explorer Archers, and the Bow Master entry records the same quirk. [sources: https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Marksman/Skills ; https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%8B%A0%EA%B6%81(%EB%A9%94%EC%9D%B4%ED%94%8C%EC%8A%A4%ED%86%A0%EB%A6%AC)]

MARKSMAN ARRIVES AT HIGH CRIT RATE LARGELY ON ITS OWN. Grandis Library's base-stats-from-skills summary for Marksman totals +75% Critical Rate from passives and buffs before gear, links or legion. Contributing skills on the wiki include Critical Shot (+40% at max), Sharp Eyes (+20%, plus +5% from the Sharp Eyes - Critical Chance hyper passive), Bullseye Shot (+20% for its duration) and the class's own link skill (+15%, which the wiki notes applies multiplicatively). Snipe, Perfect Shot and Surge Bolt additionally carry +100% bonus critical rate on their own hits, and Evasion Boost makes attacks in the second after a successful dodge critical. This is why crit rate reads as a mid-priority line rather than a starving one - the payoff is the Vicious Shot conversion, not reaching the cap. [sources: https://grandislibrary.com/explorers/marksman ; https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Marksman/Skills]

A CLASS MECHANIC THAT CHANGES SETUP RATHER THAN GEAR: Perfect Shot (KMS name True Sniping) is aimed with the mouse - the skill description instructs the player to attack with the left mouse button and cancel with the right. NamuWiki's KMS page calls this out as a mechanism unique to Marksman among all classes, in a game otherwise played from the keyboard during boss fights. Worth surfacing to a player coming from Bow Master. [sources: https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Marksman/Skills ; https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%8B%A0%EA%B6%81(%EB%A9%94%EC%9D%B4%ED%94%8C%EC%8A%A4%ED%86%A0%EB%A6%AC)]

commonMistakes.mistake: Firing the big burst skills without Split Shot running.
commonMistakes.why: Split Shot's own description makes Full Burst Shot split into extra arrows only while Split Shot is active, and the list of skills it triggers off includes Final Aim (the Origin skill) and Repeating Crossbow Cartridge. NamuWiki's KMS page calls Split Shot the skill 'which takes up most of the damage' and attributes a 20-30% overall damage loss at Suu to losing roughly half its uptime; the class quick-guide infographic independently flags Split Shot as the highest-priority skill node for both bossing and levelling. (Wording tightened 2026-09-12: the earlier phrasing said NamuWiki states the difference is large 'even for those burst skills', which is more specific than what the page says.)

commonMistakes.mistake: Sinking nodestone rolls into Covering Fire.
commonMistakes.why: CORRECTED 2026-09-12. The class quick-guide infographic lists Covering Fire as the third slot of the secondary trio and annotates it '(Useless)', which does support the mistake. The Grandis citation that used to sit beside it did NOT: Grandis files Covering Fire + Swift Surge under SECONDARY, and its legend says 'Nodes categorized as Primary and Secondary are recommended to be upgraded'. Grandis's OTHER band - 'do not need to be upgraded or has least priority' - is empty for Marksman. So the Grandis page contradicts this mistake rather than supporting it, and is now recorded as a counter-source.
commonMistakes.notes: This is an internal disagreement inside one source family - LoliFox's infographic calls Covering Fire useless while the Grandis page, also credited to the Marksman Discord, recommends upgrading it. Present it as a judgement call, not as settled advice. mastermysty lists Covering Fire in Trio #2 without comment and so is silent either way.

differencesFromBowMaster.detail: Marksman's main trio is Snipe / Piercing Arrow / Bolt Burst; the same cross-class reference gives Bow Master's as Hurricane / Arrow Blaster / Quiver Cartridge. No skill overlaps between the two main trios.

Marksman's own recommendation puts Attack Speed +1 first; the Bow Master entry in this dataset records Boss Damage +20% first. maplestorywiki's cross-class inner ability guide lists both rules as parallel bullets - 'Attack Speed: for many Explorer classes which do not have a Hurricane-like skill' and 'Boss Damage: for burst-focused classes'. Bow Master has Hurricane, so only the Boss Damage bullet applies to it and the guide is decisive there. Marksman satisfies BOTH bullets (no Hurricane-like skill, but burst-focused), so the guide does not decide the Marksman case - corrected 2026-09-12, an earlier version of this file presented the rule as predicting the split cleanly.

differencesFromBowMaster.claim: The crit-past-cap quirk is NOT a difference.
differencesFromBowMaster.detail: Vicious Shot is shared by both Explorer Archers, so the 'keep buying crit rate past 100%' advice applies identically to Marksman.

differencesFromBowMaster.claim: Sourcing quality is much worse for Marksman.
differencesFromBowMaster.detail: Bow Master has a maintained class document (Book of Bowmaster) and an independently written Dexless guide. Marksman has no public class document at all - Grandis Library's Marksman page carries no 'Class Doc' link, unlike its Bow Master page, and credits its judgement fields to the Marksman Discord directly. Every piece of Marksman node, HEXA and inner ability judgement traces to one Discord. Present Marksman advice with visibly lower confidence than Bow Master advice.

sources.note: CHARACTERISATION CORRECTED 2026-09-12. This file previously described the page as 'backed by the author's own trio-probability testing, so it is a genuine second opinion on trios'. The only methodology the page states is a simulation of the odds of FINDING all trios within 200 nodes (10,000 tests per class, May 14th 2024) - that is testing about node-drop probability, not about which skills belong in a trio. The page states no provenance at all for its trio SELECTIONS and asks readers to DM corrections, so its lists may well descend from the same class Discords. It is still counted as a second source (different author, different site, published independently), but the 'genuine second opinion' framing overstated it. conflicts.positionB: Boss Damage (Legendary, up to 20%) is the most preferred Legendary top line; Critical Rate belongs in the second or third line and moves up to the first line only if the player is not investing heavily in abilities. Attack speed is not discussed as a target line at all.
conflicts.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-12. This note previously explained the disagreement away as 'plausibly a region difference', on the grounds that Grandis labels inner ability recommendations by attack-speed-cap region and the Marksman page omits that label. There is no such labelling convention - the Grandis inner-ability data has an optional `name` field used only for 'For Bossing' / 'For Training' (verified on the Bow Master page), and no region or attack-speed field exists on either page. With that support removed, the region hypothesis is a bare guess and is retained only as such. A GMS-vs-KMS attack-speed-cap difference remains a plausible cause, but nothing in either source says so. Do not present either position as settled without the Marksman Discord confirming which applies to GMS v.271.

conflicts.topic: Composition of the secondary boost node trio
conflicts.note: This entry compared the infographic's Secondary Trio against the Grandis page's boost-node table and read the difference as a disagreement. It is not one. The Grandis page publishes BOTH structures: a recommended-trio block, which states the Secondary Trio as High Speed Shot / Arrow Illusion, Final Attack: Crossbow, Covering Fire - identical to the infographic, pairing included - and a separate table of the six boost nodes as the game actually groups them, in which Final Attack: Crossbow and High Speed Shot share node 4 and Covering Fire shares node 5 with Swift Surge. One is a recommendation, the other is an inventory of what exists. Both were re-read on 2026-09-12 and they are consistent. The real residual disagreement inside this source family is about Covering Fire's WORTH, not the trio's composition, and it is recorded on vMatrix.trios[1].caveat and commonMistakes[1].

contest.outOfScopeNote: None of the nine contested defects concerned jobs 1-4 skill builds, skill damage coefficients, damage lines, job tiers or rotations. This file carries no skillBuilds, damageLine, tier or rotation sections at all, so there was no out-of-scope content to leave alone.
priorDefectsForReference: THE BOOST NODE TIERS ARE REPORTED BACKWARDS. The Grandis Marksman page's own page data reads "primary":[0,1,2,3],"secondary":[4,5] - Nodes 1-4 are PRIMARY (Snipe; Piercing Arrow; Bolt Burst+Frostprey; Final Attack: Crossbow+High Speed Shot), Nodes 5-6 are SECONDARY (Covering Fire+Swift Surge; Arrow Blow+Arrow Illusion), and the OTHER tier is empty for Marksman. The file states in three places that Bolt Burst/Frostprey sits "one tier below Snipe and Piercing Arrow" (false - same tier), that Final Attack: Crossbow + High Speed Shot is in Grandis's "second tier" (false - Primary), and that Covering Fire is in "its lowest tier" (Secondary is the lower of two used tiers, but see next item). The error propagates into vMatrix entries 3, 4 and 5, trios[1].notes, commonMistakes[1], conflicts[1] and sources[0].

GRANDIS'S TIERS ARE NOT A DAMAGE-PRIORITY RANKING. The page's own Boost Node Legend defines PRIMARY as "Boost Nodes that unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery and are skills that are frequently used", SECONDARY as "Boost Nodes that don't unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery but are still used", OTHER as "do not need to be upgraded or has least priority", and states that "Nodes categorized as Primary and Secondary are recommended to be upgraded". The file treats the tiers as a priority ordering throughout. This also means Grandis's Primary set is exactly the set of nodes gating HEXA mastery cores 1-4 - a sourced rationale for node priority that the file missed entirely.

commonMistakes[1] ("Sinking nodestone rolls into Covering Fire") cites the Grandis page as supporting evidence, but Grandis puts Covering Fire in SECONDARY and explicitly says Primary and Secondary nodes are recommended to be upgraded. The Grandis citation contradicts the mistake rather than supporting it; the only remaining support is the infographic, which I could not read.

innerAbility.notes claims "Grandis Library normally splits recommended inner ability into bossing and training and labels it by attack-speed-cap region". No such region labelling exists. The Grandis inner-ability data structure carries only an optional name field, used as "For Bossing" / "For Training" (verified on the Bow Master page); there is no region or attack-speed-cap field anywhere in the schema or on either page. This invented convention is the sole basis for the conflicts[0] note's "likely a region artefact" explanation of the contested top line, so that explanation has no support. The other half of the sentence - that Grandis normally splits bossing/training and the Marksman page does not - is correct.

innerAbility.alternatives[0].why says NamuWiki "ranks this second among the lines to chase, after boss damage". The page says the opposite reference point: abnormal-status damage is lower in importance than crit rate and is therefore targeted as the 2nd priority AFTER CRIT RATE ("lower importance than crit rate, so it is targeted second after crit rate"). Boss damage is not the anchor.

gearingNotes glosses the Vicious Shot exclusion as "(the skill's own additional crit rate is excluded from the conversion)". Vicious Shot grants no crit rate of its own. The wiki line "The attack's additional Critical Rate is not applied" means per-attack Bonus Critical Rate - Snipe, Perfect Shot, Surge Bolt and Greater Empowered Arrows each carry Bonus Critical Rate: 100% - does not feed the conversion. This matters for a planner: the conversion runs off the character's actual crit-rate stat, which strengthens the file's conclusion but for a different mechanism than the one written down.

sources[9] claims MapleDoro's inner ability is "character-for-character identical to the Grandis / Marksman Discord list (Attack Speed +1 / Crit Rate +20% / Boss Damage +10%)". MapleDoro actually lists two lines - Legendary Attack Speed +1 and Unique Crit Rate +20% - and splits them across Bossing and Mobbing. No Boss Damage +10% line. The conclusion (rule it out as a corroborating source) may still be right; the evidence given for it is not.

sources[4] characterises mystyjl as "backed by the author's own trio-probability testing, so it is a genuine second opinion on trios". The page's only stated methodology is the odds of FINDING all trios within 200 nodes (10,000 simulations per class, dated May 14th 2024). It states no provenance whatsoever for which skills belong in each trio, and invites corrections by DM. Probability-of-finding testing is not evidence about trio selection, so the claim of an independent second opinion is unsupported - the trio lists may well descend from the same class Discords.
sources[0] describes the Grandis node table as "six two-skill nodes". Nodes 1 and 2 are single-skill (Snipe alone; Piercing Arrow alone); only nodes 3-6 pair two skills.

clearedOnInspection: NO fabricated skill or node names were found. Every name in the file checks out against maplestorywiki.net/w/Marksman/Skills and/or the Grandis node table: Bolt Burst (3rd job), Frostprey (3rd job), Covering Fire (2nd job), Swift Surge (2nd job), Arrow Blow (1st job), Arrow Illusion (4th job), Final Attack: Crossbow (2nd job), High Speed Shot (hyper active, Lv 160), Split Shot, Perfect Shot, Surge Bolt, Repeating Crossbow Cartridge, Vicious Shot, Final Aim (Origin), Fatal Trigger (Ascent), the six HEXA mastery names, and the four HEXA Enhancement boosts. The hyper passive and hyper active lists, the link skill values (MC +50% / Crit +15% / Damage +6% at Lv 9, multiplicative, stacks 3, Damage component at Lv 7), Vicious Shot 21%->50%, the Split Shot trigger list, the HEXA Piercing Arrow -> HEXA Snipe passive (+60 to +132 percentage points at Lv 30), Grandis's +75% crit from skills, and the legion crit 1/2/3/4/5% all match their cited sources exactly. What follows are asserted claims contradicted by, or absent from, the sources cited for them.
contest.shipReadyNote: Scoped to the five endgame sections (vMatrix, hexa, hyperSkills, hyperStats, innerAbility). Every claim in them was re-read against its cited page on 2026-09-12 and now carries sources, sourceCount, consensus and verifiedAt. Nothing in this file is labelled 'strong' - Marksman has no source family beyond the Marksman Discord plus, per topic, one of NamuWiki KMS or mastermysty, so three independent sources are never available. That is an accurate label, not a gap in the work.

writtenNote: The five endgame sections contain no unverified claim. What they DO contain, deliberately, are several accurately-labelled absences: hyperStats.priority is null, hyperSkills.actives is null, vMatrix.priority and vMatrix.levelOrder are null, the per-node HEXA order is not transcribed, and the infographic's skill-node icon chain is not transcribed. Those are gaps recorded as gaps, which is the correct state for them. Consumers MUST respect vMatrix.priorityOrdered:false, vMatrix.nodeBands[].ordered:false, vMatrix.trios[].ordered:false and hyperSkills.*.ordered:false - array position in those fields carries no priority meaning. Only innerAbility.lines is ordered (linesOrdered:true), because the quick-guide infographic prints the lines numbered 1st/2nd/3rd. The one unresolved substantive question, the GMS-vs-KMS inner ability top line, is recorded in conflicts[0] and reflected in that line's contested:true and weak rankConsensus rather than being presented as settled.
